entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lieutenant-General Charles Schaw Cathcart, 9th Lord Cathcart, KT, (died 1776) was a distinguished Scottish peer, soldier, and diplomat whose career spanned significant geopolitical shifts of the mid-18th century. As chief of the ancient Clan Cathcart, he embodied a lineage deeply intertwined with Scottish history, yet his most impactful contributions were on the broader European and nascent global stage. His service as a senior British Army officer during the War of the Austrian Succession and the Seven Years' War, coupled with his pivotal diplomatic posting as Ambassador to Russia, positioned him at the confluence of military strategy and international relations during an era of imperial expansion and shifting alliances.

Cathcart's military career began with the Scots Fusiliers, seeing action at the Battle of Fontenoy in 1745 during the War of the Austrian Succession and later at the Battle of Minden in 1759, a decisive British victory in the Seven Years' War. Rising through the ranks, he achieved the distinguished position of Lieutenant-General. His diplomatic zenith came with his appointment as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the Court of Catherine the Great in Russia from 1768 to 1771. During this critical posting, he navigated complex Anglo-Russian relations, particularly concerning the First Partition of Poland and the ongoing Russo-Turkish War, successfully securing a commercial treaty in 1766 that bolstered British trade interests and influence in the Baltic and Black Sea regions.
